abstract: Traction force microscopy is a simple, non-invasive method that can quantify cellular contact forces at the cell-substrate interface. It solves an inverse problem of determining the force field from measured substrate deformation. Because this problem is ill-posed with a large condition number, it is necessary to suppress the amplification of measurement noise during inversion. Previous studies have employed algorithms such as regularization or filtering that utilize spatial information to discriminate noise and true signals. Here, we propose an alternative approach that utilizes temporal information of the system. This method employs Kalman filter, a simple data assimilation algorithm in time series analysis, to recover the force field. Using numerically generated data, we show that the method is more accurate than standard algorithms including L2-regularization and is effective at filtering out temporal noise. Using experimental data on locomoting cells, we demonstrate that the method can reliably infer time-varying cellular traction forces. We also demonstrate two extensions of the proposed method: incorporation of additional knowledge and direct inference of low-dimensional force characteristics. These practical advantages will motivate the use of proposed framework for analyzing dynamic cell mechanics.
